description: Laying out and filling an all-over repeating ground pattern on paper before tooling. Construction lines are folded and marked into the paper to divide it into equal cells, then a few tools are impressed at fixed crossing points so the same simple motif repeats predictably over the whole surface.
name: building a diaper pattern

source_ref.label: Douglas Cockerell, Bookbinding and the Care of Books (1901), Chapter XVI, p.235. Internet Archive.
Douglas Cockerell, Bookbinding and the Care of Books (D. Appleton, 1901), Internet Archive

steps.description: Cut a piece of thin paper to the size of the board and pencil a margin line a short distance inside the edge all round.
Find the centre construction lines by folding the paper side to side and head to tail, then crease the remaining division lines with the point of a folder.
Join the crossing points and re-cross as needed until the cells are reduced to the desired size, keeping every space the same shape.
Impress a flower tool at the chosen line crossings, reheating it in candle smoke between a few impressions.
Add a short straight-line stalk below each flower and place a leaf to each side to complete the repeating unit.
